body.statement:
For each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their conditional joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_q
\quad\text{on }\mathcal Z_+,
\]
where \(R_q\) uses \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in the spacing channel.  The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen with uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.  For the random-spacing pair only positive testing affinity is asserted.  Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel; in particular, its event means are stable given the complete historical design and its historical errors are centered given that design.
body.justification: All four pairs are completed as causal panels in the full-design-centered subclass, with both strong conditional-mean restrictions verified directly.
body.gap: The spacing experiment is certified by positive affinity on a no-active-block event; bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence is deliberately not claimed for it.
body.consumer: The minimax and interval lower bounds therefore apply to the causal panel rather than an auxiliary fixed-query experiment.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a regular conditional law given \(E_0\), and write
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
All constants below are chosen inside the nonempty interior of the fixed support, variance, Holder, covariance, and modulus envelopes.  The query is placed in a fixed compact subset of the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\), contained in \(\mathcal Z_+\).  Event outcomes are drawn independently of \(\mathscr X\), and, conditional on \(\mathscr X\), historical errors are drawn independently across units with conditional mean zero.  Thus
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{1}
\]
Unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes are completed so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Setting observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, and making every potential outcome independent of other units' assignments, verifies consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and event transport.  Bounded Bernoulli response kernels with probabilities in a fixed compact subset of \((0,1)\) verify boundedness and the conditional-variance lower bound.  The donor sample is conditionally iid, independent of the panel, with covariance in the declared ellipticity interval and standardized fourth moment within its envelope.  Finally set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Hence every experiment constructed below is a regular conditional law in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and (1) verifies the two additional full-design restrictions directly.

We first record an elementary binary divergence bound.  If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), Taylor's formula for
\(x\mapsto x\log(x/p)+(1-x)\log\{(1-x)/(1-p)\}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le \frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{2}
\]
Conditional independence makes the divergence of the response product the sum of the conditional binary divergences.

For the treated channel put \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and change the event Bernoulli mean in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Because \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge \pi_s^2/n_s\), one has \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\), so all probabilities remain in the fixed interior interval along the stated arrays.  The target separation is
\[
\sum_s\pi_sv_s
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{-1/2}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\tag{3}
\]
whereas (2) bounds the joint divergence by
\[
C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{4}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and set
\[
b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
For a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump \(\psi\) with \(\psi(0)=1\), perturb only cohort \(s_*\) by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{5}
\]
Take \(c_1\) small enough to preserve the response interior, the Holder radius, and the two-sided local modulus.  For \(\lambda>1\) use a common affine carrier with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient; for \(0<\lambda\le1\) use a common asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier.  The perturbation is small in the relevant Holder norm, so the carrier's lower modulus remains bounded away from zero.  Since \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\left|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)\right|^2
=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The perturbation is supported on a set of design probability at most \(Cb^d\).  Integrating (2) over the design and summing over the \(Tn_{s_*}\) responses gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{7}
\]

For the spacing channel use the pair in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  Its construction obeys (1), all one-time density bounds, and the frozen geometric mixing envelope; its observed laws coincide on the no-active-block event of probability at least a fixed positive constant.  Its squared target separation is at least
\[
c\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus this pair has positive testing affinity.  No bounded Kullback--Leibler assertion is made for it.

For the donor channel retain the affine carrier when \(\lambda>1\) and the asymmetric cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  By the lower half of the local-modulus condition, for \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\le\delta_0\) there is an admissible direction \(u_N\), or a direction attaining half the supremum, such that
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2\le c_2N^{-1/2},
\qquad
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose a fixed common-support finite-dimensional donor submodel whose probability vector is tilted by order \(N^{-1/2}\) in the direction \(\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\).  The tilt can be chosen inside the covariance and fourth-moment envelopes; its score is bounded and has nonsingular information.  A direct Taylor expansion of the finite probability-vector likelihood gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete the untreated event potential outcomes under each law with means \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (9) into the target separation, whose square is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

It remains only to translate (4), (7), and (10) into affinity.  For any two laws let \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), \(p=P_1(A)\), and \(q=P_0(A)\).  Applying Jensen's inequality separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\), and differentiating the resulting binary divergence twice, yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
\ge2(p-q)^2.
\]
Since \(p-q=\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (11) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and donor pairs; (8) supplies affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (2) verify membership in the full-design-centered class for all four pairs, which proves the claim.
